Every day, people face emergencies they were never trained for. A fire, a flood, a deep cut, a heart that stops.
For example: a man collapses. His heart has stopped.
Every minute without CPR, his chance of survival drops by up to ten percent.
The person next to him wants to help, but has never done this before.
On the phone, the dispatcher can guide them. But they can't see a thing.
With AI glasses from Meta, one tap raises the alert, and the dispatcher sees exactly what the witness sees.
A voice guide checks if he responds and breathes, then starts CPR on the beat. Hands stay on the chest.
The dispatcher takes over, and corrects the hands in real time.
And it's not only cardiac arrest. Severe bleeding, choking, an earthquake, a tsunami: FirstFive is built to guide anyone through the first minutes of any emergency.
When the ambulance arrives, the handover report is already waiting.
Consent first. Recording only during an emergency. Built on Meta's Device Access Toolkit.
Bystander CPR can more than double survival. In any emergency, FirstFive makes sure help starts in time.
FirstFive. Any emergency. The first five minutes, together.
